rule: While staging, the gateway answers initialize, ping and discovery (tools/list, resources/list, resources/templates/list, prompts/list) with empty lists, queues other requests, and removes canceled requests before dispatch. It handshakes with the native server, replays outstanding requests in order, announces list changes so clients refetch the native catalog, and relays frames. Failed staging answers queued and later requests, discovery included, with -32603. A discover-first (modern) client gets no warm replies. When a previously published usable server exists the gateway serves from it before staging ends; a refresh that changed it is swapped in by handshaking a new server with the client's original initialize params, routing new requests to it, letting the replaced server finish its in-flight requests (its other frames are dropped and logged) and then ending it. A failed refresh is logged and serving continues; an unchanged refresh does nothing. A relayed typed missing-model refusal (schema 📦️component-models) makes the gateway ask its launcher to build that plugin's component model once per plugin and session, one build at a time and cancelled when the session ends; a build that changed the published model set swaps a freshly handshaken server in behind the client, a failed build is logged and retried by the next refusal, and until a build succeeds the relayed refusals of that plugin carry the build failure (cause model-build-failed, its reason) instead of the promise that the model is being prepared. An unexpected exit of the serving native server while ready (non-zero status or a signal) answers its held requests with a retryable -32603 error naming the exit, restarts the server through the refresh handshake while staging continues, queues requests meanwhile and announces list changes; restarts are bounded by a budget within a time window, beyond which, like a clean exit, the session ends.
